source_contract.release_pattern: load all dense bool masks and refs, then dict-comprehension all int64 nonzero indices while retaining masks
source_contract.streaming_repair_pattern: load same artifact, process mask tensors smallest-first, derive int64 nonzero indices, pop/release each dense mask immediately; retain refs + indices + key membership only

byte_model.release_steady_aux: N + 12s bytes (bool dense mask + fp32 refs + int64 indices)
byte_model.steady_saving: N bytes exactly for the masked tensor domain, independent of support fraction
byte_model.initial_after_torch_load: N + 4s bytes before index materialization, ignoring serialization/Python overhead
byte_model.streaming_peak_lower_bound: max(N+4s, 12s) plus at most one tensor's temporary index-before-mask-release term; processing smaller tensors first reduces transient peak

scope: This is a source-equivalent synthetic memory-lifetime benchmark, not a TRL/DeepSpeed run.
ru_maxrss contains Python/Torch process baseline and allocator behavior; logical tensor bytes are the cleaner scaling quantity.
No explicit gc.collect was needed for the lower-peak 10% streaming run; Python refcount/tensor destruction released mask objects sufficiently in this CPU test.
The 33.3% run used every third position, not an exact 35% support case.
Real CPO mask-domain/support, CUDA/CPU-offload allocator behavior and PyTorch 2.8 remain unmeasured.
